page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at 3.9 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache. The system includes 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2110.0 and high single-threaded compression speeds, such as 34.08 GB/sec in gzip compression. However, multi-core performance is relatively weaker, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 4301.36 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 27.63 GB/sec. Memory performance is mixed; while large-block read and write bandwidths are average, small-block cached read bandwidth and the PassMark memory score fall into the lower tier.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile, the c8i-flex.xlarge offers a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring high single-thread performance without massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, software compilation, and basic database operations. It is less optimal for memory-intensive applications or highly parallelized multi-threaded workloads due to its memory capacity limits and lower multi-core benchmark scaling.
